cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: A Kinder Version
cards.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nina's dinner is just a small group. Let's make another plan; I'll book us noodles.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's invited the whole choir. Read me the message.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We don't need to read an invitation like a rejection letter. She wants an uncomplicated evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm in that choir. Does the message say I'm complicated?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, I'm not reading that bit aloud. We're dealing with one dinner, not grading your whole personality. Let me book somewhere we'll both enjoy.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 offers a softened small-dinner account; A3 corrects B2's interpretation as rejection; A5 treats B4's self-label as an overbroad personality judgment and offers a safer shared evening.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 whole-choir fact defeats smallness, so A3 shifts to uncomplicated evening. B4 identifies the implied label; A5 refuses the hurtful wording and redirects its scope to one dinner.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 reasonably seek the text and challenge explanations against belonging to the choir. A's protective approach can fail to soothe without making B implausible.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's self-directed complicated question to move from edited explanation to explicit protection and concrete company.

specificity.evidence: A1 Nina dinner and noodles, B2 whole choir and B4 B's membership make the exclusion legible.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 has a refusal, a scope correction and a company offer; each addresses the text, interpretation and immediate evening, without adding a joke.

coach2.stated: A1 says small group; B2 whole choir invited; B4 belongs to choir; A5 declines reading part of the message aloud.
coach2.inferred: A is deliberately editing a hurtful message to protect B, not giving a consistent objective guest count.
coach2.missing: The precise insult can stay unrevealed because B4 has already identified its emotional direction.
coach2.firstDefect: No failed gate; A's changing explanations are a legible protective tactic, not accidental contradictory world facts.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 contradicts A1's small-dinner account and asks for the message.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 substitutes a kinder characterization after B2 demands the text.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 tests the implication of A3's uncomplicated wording against B's choir membership.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 refuses to voice the hurtful bit and corrects B4's whole-person interpretation while offering company.
